Full summary: Implemented #46: TWINING_PROJECT env var for shared stores — resolution --project arg > env > cwd (relative env values resolve against cwd), plugin 1.17.0 drops its hardcoded --project . which would have shadowed the env var. Verified end-to-end with the built binary.
Decisions: Chose to pair the server-side TWINING_PROJECT support with removing --project . from the plugin launch command — the issue's proposed precedence (arg > env > cwd) is correct, but the plugin's hardcoded --project . would have permanently shadowed the env var for exactly the server the issue targets; cwd default is behavior-identical when the var is unset. Rejected shell-expanding ${TWINING_PROJECT:-.} inside the plugin's sh -lc string — works today but buries resolution logic in a shell one-liner instead of one canonical, testable code path.; Chose to resolve relative TWINING_PROJECT values against the server cwd while passing explicit --project values through verbatim — preserves the pre-#46 arg contract exactly (no regression) while giving env users predictable semantics; absolute paths documented as recommended for multi-machine setups.
Findings: Plugin 1.17.0 (no --project arg) is safe against 2.1.0 servers — cwd default is identical — but TWINING_PROJECT itself needs a server >= 2.2 release to take effect. The env-var feature is inert for users until the next server tag is pushed.; The #42 dashboard single-instance guard composes well with shared stores: sibling repos pointing at one TWINING_PROJECT resolve the same projectRoot, so only the first session hosts the dashboard and the rest stay MCP-only — exactly the wanted behavior for the fleet use case.
